Hi Ellis — thanks for the quick read. A few operational clarifications that should help: 

- Lead registration: Redwood's standard is that a HubSpot lead record with "partner-registered" status plus a short registration form (attached helps) is sufficient. We do, however, require that the registered lead hasn't been actively engaged by a Redwood AE prior to registration. The 12-month window applies to net-new customer revenue attributable to the registered opportunity. If the opportunity evolves product-wise (e.g., from hosted API to Dedicated), we still treat it as registered provided the core account/company is the same legal entity.

- Exclusivity ask: Camila's initial note was intended to be narrow. We're willing to accept a right-of-first-refusal (ROFR) rather than hard exclusivity in the named verticals — 6 months is reasonable; Ellis' suggestion of 9 months for >$100k ARR deals is acceptable if we confirm a mutual lead-intake SLA. We also propose a mutual 'no-hire' clause for reps specifically assigned to the co-sell pilot for the first 6 months.

- Net revenue definition: Net revenue = gross subscription + usage less discounts, credits, refunds, payment processor fees. Platform fees (marketplace margins) are excluded where applicable. Quarterly audit right is fine for material sums; we suggest an annual reconciliation as the default with a single additional audit triggered if variance >5% or total revshare exceeds $250k in a rolling 12 months. Redwood covers the first $2,500 of audit costs; additional costs split pro rata.

I attached a short "partner lead registration" form and some sample RevShare calculations (examples-revshare-calcs.xlsx) so you can see the math on MRU/ARR scenarios.

If those items look good, Ben and I can draft a short MOU and either legal can take a pass. Happy to do a 30m on Friday if that works for you.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — that clears up a lot. Couple follow-ups: 

1) Lead intake SLA: Integral can promise a 48h response to inbound opportunities registered via HubSpot and to surface a named AE within 5 business days. Can Redwood commit to not engaging a registered lead for 7 calendar days to give our team a chance to qualify?

2) ROFR timeline: We prefer the 9-month ROFR on $100k+ deals. If Redwood takes the lead post-ROFR and converts, Integral would still receive the referral share on any revenue attributable to introductions we made during the ROFR period.

3) Payment cadence: Net 45 after monthly reconciliation is preferred. Can you confirm Redwood's payout cadence?

I’ll attach our partner order/process doc as promised — sending now.

— Ellis

- Payout cadence: Redwood pays partners monthly, net 30 following the month of record; we can accommodate Net 45 for the pilot with a one-off finance memo.

Camila
